title: The leaking basket
hookLine: Abba Moses, asked to judge a brother, carries a leaking basket of sand: my sins run out behind me
tomorrow: a monk does every prayer on his list. what else is there to do?

cards: A group chat can turn into a courtroom fast: screenshots as evidence, everyone weighing in, a verdict by lunch. The desert monks of Scetis had their own version.
A brother has done something wrong, and they call a meeting to deal with him. They send for Abba Moses, an elder they respect. He won't come.
They send again: everyone is waiting for you. So he gets up and goes. But he brings something slung over his shoulder, and it's leaving a trail.

teach.h: ABBA AND AMMA OF THE DESERT.
teach.b: This story comes from the sayings of the desert fathers and mothers, monks and nuns who went out to live simply and pray. Their elders were called abba, father, and amma, mother.
Abba Moses walks in carrying a basket full of sand, and the basket leaks. Sand runs out behind him the whole way. Some tellings make it a cracked jug of water; the picture is the same.
The others ask: father, what is this?

teach.h: MY SINS RUN OUT BEHIND ME.
teach.b: And he says, in the sense of the saying: my sins are running out behind me, and I don't see them, and today I've come to judge someone else's. No speech.
One basket and one sentence. And the story ends quietly: they say nothing more to the brother, and they forgive him. Look where the sand is.
Behind him, out of his sight. Jesus asks the same thing with a splinter and a plank: "why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?"

how: The sayings of the desert fathers and mothers are read by Orthodox, Catholic and Protestant Christians, often one short saying at a time, as food for prayer.

o: Abba Moses's sand: his own faults trailing behind
a punishment desert monks gave to rule-breakers
a basket monks used to collect food in villages

games.q: the desert meeting — tap the pairs.
p: the desert where the brother lived

s: the desert monks were stern judges who loved to expose sin
asked to judge, Abba Moses carried his own leaking faults, and the brother was forgiven.
the desert elders were called abba, father, and amma, mother.
some tellings make the basket a leaking jug of water
the picture is the same: faults running out behind, unseen.

games.q: at work, everyone's lining up to complain about a teammate who botched a big order. your manager asks what you think should happen. what would Abba Moses bring to that meeting?
o: his own leaking basket: a reminder of his own faults.
a list of the teammate's past mistakes.
a vote on the right punishment.
games.why: Abba Moses came to the trial carrying sand that ran out behind him: my sins, unseen, and I've come to judge another's. the meeting ended in forgiveness.

practice: If you can, walk slowly across the room and back, and with each step picture a little sand trailing behind you, your own trail you can't quite see.
Then bring to mind someone you've been quick to judge lately, and set the verdict down for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: The leaking basket. Abba Moses's answer to a call to judge: walking in with his own faults trailing behind him.

orig.note: Aramaic for father, written in Greek letters in Romans 8:15; the desert elders' title.

carryVoice: Keep this one: my own sins trail behind, out of sight and still falling. Two weeks, done.
